nodes.label: Administrator
nodes.rationale: A server-side fact about an account, carried on the sign-in response and remembered with the profile, so only as fresh as the last sign-in — an offline resume keeps the previous answer. Admin controls are drawn for nobody else because each would earn a refusal from the server.

nodes.label: Auth key
nodes.rationale: Kavita's non-expiring opds key: the one secret a profile keeps, signing in with no password and authenticating image URLs. The JWT it mints is session state and is never written down. It is a whole account, so a device holding four profiles holds four complete account credentials (ADR-0004).

nodes.label: Avatar
nodes.rationale: Fetched by account id, never by file name; with none, or no key left to fetch it with, the face falls back to the profile's initial on its colour.

nodes.label: Catalogue
nodes.rationale: What the device remembers of a profile's shelves: libraries, the series in them, and the parts of series looked inside. It names what exists and never holds a page — the whole line between it and a saved chapter, which is content. It belongs to the profile because what a person may see is the server's answer to them alone. Every entry is refetchable, so it is discardable by design: the worst a wrong one costs is one refresh, which is why it is never migrated and never repaired. 'Cache' is spoken for by the image cache.

nodes.label: Chapter
nodes.rationale: The reading unit: what a row opens and what reading progress attaches to. Named in the library type's own vocabulary — an issue in a comic library, a book in a book library — never as a bare 'chapter'.

nodes.label: Continue (the promotion)
nodes.rationale: One series, not a set: the one read most recently that is started and unfinished. Picked out of On deck rather than fetched, so one request answers both and the card and shelf can never disagree. Kavita's 'currently reading' route is NOT this concept — it filters ReadLast GreaterThan OnDeckProgressDays, which SeriesFilter.HasReadLast inverts into MaxDate < now - N, i.e. On deck's complement, so promoting from it left regular readers with no promotion at all.

nodes.label: Credential
nodes.rationale: A password the first time, an auth key every time after — never both and never neither, which is why it is a sealed type in code: the wire format cannot express the choice, so the client does.

nodes.label: Device default
nodes.rationale: What a profile that has never chosen a preference reads in: the value under the flat key this device held before it had profiles. For the language it is also what the gate is drawn in, since the picker stands in front of every session and has nobody to ask — choosing a language moves it, and that is the only preference it is true of.

nodes.label: Face
nodes.rationale: One profile on the picker — avatar or initial, name, and server where more than one is remembered. Called a face and not a row because it is what a person recognises themselves by.

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.rationale: The screen a device with no session lands on. Which one it is is a rule about the device rather than a screen's own decision, so the app has exactly one place that decides it.

nodes.label: Handover
nodes.rationale: A switch followed by somebody else's arrival: the app is built again on a container of its own so nothing a provider held for the previous person can reach the next. It is neither a launch (the splash does not play) nor a resume.

nodes.label: Image cache
nodes.rationale: Covers and pages kept on disk merely because they were looked at online: fills on its own, is capped, and the OS may reclaim it. Not the offline library and never counted as one. It belongs to the device and is shared by every profile — one budget, one copy of a cover however many people look at that series.

nodes.label: Issue
nodes.rationale: What a chapter is called in a Comic or ComicVine library, always written with the number sign (Issue #12).

nodes.label: Kavita (the server)
nodes.rationale: The server owns files, metadata and reading progress and is the authority on all three; Patra deliberately reuses Kavita's nouns because a client that renames the server's concepts ends up speaking a different language from the thing it browses.

nodes.label: Library
nodes.rationale: Built from a folder and carrying a type; its contents are whatever the last scan found, so it drifts from the folder as the folder changes. An empty library means no scan has yet found anything there.

nodes.label: Library type
nodes.rationale: One of Kavita's six kinds (Manga, Comic, Book, Image, Light Novel, ComicVine). It decides what a series is made of and what every part of it is called, so it is never cosmetic.

nodes.label: Link (deep link)
nodes.rationale: Names something to read — a series or a chapter and nothing else. It says what to open and not who is reading, so on a device with faces it waits for one; it opens on top of the app rather than instead of it, and is spent the first moment somebody is reading.

nodes.label: Lock
nodes.rationale: A PIN asked before a profile is entered, on this device, so it is asked offline too. It keeps out the other people who share the device and is explicitly not protection for a lost device — no copy may suggest it is. Suggested to a profile the server restricts nothing about (an administrator included, since an admin can lift their own restriction) and never to a restricted one.

nodes.label: Login result
nodes.rationale: Who you are, the auth key to keep, and a JWT to spend. Deliberately not called a session: a session is a profile the app is reading as, and this is only what one is built from.

nodes.label: Loose chapter
nodes.rationale: A chapter belonging to no volume, listed under the library type's own chapter heading alongside the volumes. Not called 'loose-leaf chapter', which names the container rather than the chapter.

nodes.label: Magnifying
nodes.rationale: A one-finger drag enlarges the page around the point pressed, as an alternative to pinching, which needs a second hand. Held rather than switched on — the page returns when the finger lifts — and off unless asked for, because it takes the swipe that turns a page. Not 'loupe': a loupe is a lens over one region, this scales the whole page.

nodes.label: Offline
nodes.rationale: The state of not being able to reach the server: a property of the app's last attempt, not of the device's radio.

nodes.label: On deck
nodes.rationale: Series with progress as Kavita picks and orders them (PagesRead > 0 && PagesRead < Pages plus a recency clause). It is the home shelf and the pool Continue is chosen from; the promoted series is removed so no series is two things on one screen. The removal is keyed on the card being there, so a series whose chapter could not be fetched stays in the list rather than leaving the screen with it.

nodes.label: Picker
nodes.rationale: Asks who is reading before anything is read, drawn entirely from what the device remembers so it appears with no network. A device holding one profile never sees it — being asked a question with one answer is a tap nobody agreed to.

nodes.label: PIN
nodes.rationale: Four digits, the only thing that opens a lock. Biometrics are asked first and the PIN is the fallback, never the other way round, and never the device's own lock-screen code, which on a shared tablet everybody already knows.

nodes.label: Preference
nodes.rationale: A setting somebody chose. Reading direction, magnifying and the interface language follow a profile; the image cache budget belongs to the device because it is disk. None is ever sent to the server. A preference nobody has chosen is not stored — the device default stands in for it.

nodes.label: Profile
nodes.rationale: One person's Kavita account on a server, remembered with its auth key and never its password. Progress, library access and age restriction belong to a profile alone because the server keeps them per account. Identity is the server address plus Kavita's own account id — never the name, which is a label the server lets its owner change.

nodes.label: Profile colour
nodes.rationale: The colour Kavita's own web UI paints an account in, carried on sign-in and remembered. It is per person and never the app's accent token, which stands for reading progress and identity. An account with none still falls back to a colour, because a face with no colour is one that fails to be told apart.

nodes.label: Pseudo-volume
nodes.rationale: The two containers Kavita invents for what does not fit the numbering — the loose-leaf volume and the specials volume. Both carry a sentinel number and neither is ever shown as a volume.

nodes.label: Reading direction
nodes.rationale: One setting with three values — left-to-right, right-to-left, vertical scrolling. The third is a direction like the other two, not a separate mode beside them. Never 'LTR'/'RTL' in anything a user reads.

nodes.label: Reading progress
nodes.rationale: Counted in pages and existing per chapter and per series, which answer different questions: finishing a volume leaves the next untouched, so whether a series is under way is not what the next chapter says.

nodes.label: Registered device
nodes.rationale: Kavita's own record of a client, one per installation, kept apart by an identifier the app generates and remembers. The app renames its own entry once per session and never touches a name a person typed in Kavita.

nodes.label: Remove
nodes.rationale: Forgetting a profile and its key while the others on its server stay. It lives in Settings because somebody must have entered a profile before they can remove any of them — the credential the picker cannot ask for.

nodes.label: Saved chapter
nodes.rationale: Pages stored on the device because a profile asked for them: chosen deliberately, never evicted, readable with no server. It belongs to the profile that saved it, so two people sharing a device do not share what each saved. 'Download' names the act of fetching one, not the thing.

nodes.label: Scan
nodes.rationale: Asked for, never finished, by the app: Kavita answers the request and does the work afterwards, so nothing the app says about a scan is ever a report of its result. Only an administrator can ask. Distinct from a refresh, which asks Kavita what it already knows — a scan is what changes the answer.

nodes.label: Series
nodes.rationale: One work — a manga, a comic run, a book — the thing a cover in the grid stands for.

nodes.label: Server (remembered address)
nodes.rationale: A Kavita address connected to at least once, remembered so it need not be typed again; several can be remembered and each holds one or more profiles.

nodes.label: Server version
nodes.rationale: Belongs to the server, not the app or the profile, and is only ever true of a server reachable right now — the moment it cannot be reached there is no version rather than an old one. 'Version' unqualified is avoided because the app has one of its own.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.rationale: Exactly one profile can be the active session, and every request the app makes is made as that one.

nodes.label: Special
nodes.rationale: A chapter Kavita flags as outside the numbered run; known by its title alone and never numbered.

nodes.label: Spine
nodes.rationale: The part of the catalogue loaded whole — the libraries and the series in each. Everything under it (a series' volumes, chapters, description) is loaded per series when that series is opened. Ours to name rather than Kavita's, because the distinction is about this device's memory and the server has no word for it.

nodes.label: Storyline
nodes.rationale: Volumes and loose chapters read as one ordered story. Only a storyline when the series has both, and only in a library type where it means something — an issue run is not a storyline.

nodes.label: Switch
nodes.rationale: Handing the app to somebody else: returns to the picker and keeps the auth key, so coming back is a tap and never a password. One of a profile's two verbs, and the only one the face on the home bar offers.

nodes.label: Vertical scrolling
nodes.rationale: Pages run as one continuous strip and are scrolled rather than turned. Kavita calls it webtoon and separately offers a paged vertical direction this app does not, which is why the word is 'scrolling' and not merely 'vertical'; on screen one word 'Vertical' suffices while it is the only vertical direction.

nodes.label: Volume
nodes.rationale: A numbered collection of chapters within a series; in a book library the volume is the book and has no chapters under it.

nodes.label: patra package manifest
nodes.rationale: Flutter client for Kavita, publish_to: none. Dependencies encode the architecture named in the docs: dio (HTTP), flutter_riverpod 3 (state), go_router (routing), flutter_secure_storage (the auth key and locks), local_auth (biometrics in front of a PIN), cached_network_image + flutter_cache_manager (image cache), package_info_plus (version read off the binary), crypto (salted PIN hashing), device_info_plus (client identity headers), flutter_slidable (chapter row panes), path_provider (saved chapters).

nodes.label: Fixed French glossary
nodes.rationale: Not a translator's choice: the series-part terms (tome, chapitre, numéro with #, livre, hors-série, arc narratif) match what Kavita itself says in French and test/entity_naming_test.dart fails if they drift. Four more (profil, serveur, verrou, code) are fixed by choice because they name the app's own furniture. Profil over compte for the same reason English avoids 'account' — on a picker showing faces the word must name a person, not a credential; code over 'code PIN' (a pleonasm) and never mot de passe, which is what a server asks for.

nodes.label: App icons generated by tool/gen_app_icons.sh, not flutter_launcher_icons
nodes.norm_label: app icons generated by tool/gen_app_icons.sh, not flutter_launcher_icons
nodes.rationale: flutter_launcher_icons rasterises a single master to every size, but anything at or under 72px must come from the compact three-blade frond because five blades close into a blob there. The script also leaves the Android adaptive icon alone — its foreground is the hand-kept vector res/drawable/patra_mark.xml.

nodes.label: pubspec version is only a local fallback
nodes.norm_label: pubspec version is only a local fallback
nodes.rationale: version: 0.1.0+1 is only the default a local build falls back to. A release takes its version from the git tag via --build-name and its build number from the CI run, and the app reads both back off the binary, so nothing in the repository can disagree with the tag that shipped.

nodes.label: LibraryTypeNaming (lib/src/entity_naming.dart)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors Kavita's EntityNamingService: a comic has issues where a manga has chapters, and a book library calls a volume a book at both levels. Never hardcode 'chapter' or 'volume' in a screen; the type comes from libraryTypeProvider(libraryId), which falls back to manga while the library list is in flight so no screen waits on it. It names only what is numbered — a title never reaches the button, because free text stretches it across the hero.

nodes.label: The fixed French glossary
nodes.rationale: specials = hors-série, volume = tome, chapter = chapitre, issue = numéro (with the croisillon, as Kavita does), storyline = arc narratif. Pinned in both languages.

nodes.label: LibraryType (Manga/Comic/Book/Image/LightNovel/ComicVine)
nodes.rationale: Decides what a series is made of and what its parts are called; Kavita words its whole series page from it.

nodes.label: Localization (app_en.arb template, app_fr.arb)
nodes.rationale: Never hardcode user-facing strings: add the key to both ARBs, run flutter gen-l10n, and use AppLocalizations.of(context) (non-nullable, configured in l10n.yaml). Generated files are committed. Widget tests run under en, and SectionLabel uppercases, so tests match 'CONTINUE'.

nodes.label: Kavita sentinel numbers (ParserConstants ±100000)
nodes.rationale: Same magnitude, opposite signs — the sign is the whole distinction, so never compare on abs(), which silently files the specials volume under loose-leaf and makes isSpecials dead code. isLooseLeaf / isSpecials / isVolumePlaceholder exist so these never reach the UI as '-100000'.

nodes.label: GET /api/Series/series-detail is deliberately not called
nodes.rationale: It returns the buckets ready-made but is documented as internal ('may change without hesitation') and its labels are pre-formatted in the server account's locale, which would fight our own fr/en. We take /api/Series/volumes and apply the rules ourselves.

nodes.label: The storyline as a section header, not a tab
nodes.norm_label: the storyline as a section header, not a tab
nodes.rationale: Kavita shows the storyline only for Manga and Image libraries; our series screen has sections, so it is the header over the volumes and the loose chapters when a series has both, and stays 'Tomes' with volumes alone. Specials always close the screen.

nodes.label: apiKey is the opds auth key, one row not a concept
nodes.community_name: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: apikey is the opds auth key, one row not a concept
nodes.rationale: AppUser.ApiKey is [Obsolete("Migrated to AuthKey in v0.8.9")] and ConstructUserDto computes dto.ApiKey = user.GetOpdsAuthKey(). If its owner rotates it from Kavita's web UI, the stored copy starts answering 401 with no other signal — exactly the stale-profile state the picker already draws (greyed, badged, asking for a password by name).

nodes.label: LoginDto ignores username/password when ApiKey is passed
nodes.community_name: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: logindto ignores username/password when apikey is passed
nodes.rationale: The password-free path is documented rather than inferred: LoginDto states it, and AccountController.Login resolves the user from the key via GetUserByAuthKey (which chains .HasNotExpired()) and skips CheckPasswordSignInAsync entirely, while still checking LoginRole and returning the complete UserDto. The credential travels in the body. KavitaClient.login already posts 'apiKey': '' — this decision is that field, filled in.

nodes.label: Token lifetimes are absent from the spec
nodes.community_name: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: token lifetimes are absent from the spec
nodes.rationale: The OpenAPI spec exposes no token lifetime at all — no expiresIn, no expiresAt, on UserDto or TokenRequestDto — so a client cannot schedule a refresh and can only react to a 401. The real numbers come from Kavita's C# source: JWT 10 days on 0.9.0.x and 3 days on 0.9.1.x; refresh token ~1 day (ASP.NET Identity's never-overridden default) on 0.9.0.x and 30 days on 0.9.1.x. On 0.9.0.x a family iPad picked up each evening would land on 'sign in again' nearly every time.

nodes.label: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.community_name: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: a profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.rationale: Entering a profile posts { username, apiKey } to /api/Account/login; the JWT that comes back is session state and is never written down. The auth key does not expire (the opds and image-only keys are created with ExpiresAtUtc = null), while persisting the pair would add two expiring secrets without removing the durable one.

nodes.label: Using the auth key as the request scheme (rejected alternative)
nodes.community_name: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: using the auth key as the request scheme (rejected alternative)
nodes.rationale: Kavita's selector ranks the auth key above bearer, so the app could authenticate every request with it — but that would drop the JWT and with it the only time-bounded credential in the design.

nodes.label: POST /api/Plugin/authenticate (rejected alternative)
nodes.community_name: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.rationale: Mints the same token pair but checks no role at all, takes the key in the query string, returns a partial UserDto with no roles or preferences, and logs the raw key in cleartext on failure.

nodes.label: refresh-token on 0.9.0.x must not be leaned on
nodes.community_name: A profile persists the auth key and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: refresh-token on 0.9.0.x must not be leaned on
nodes.rationale: It is [AllowAnonymous], reads the supplied JWT with ReadJwtToken (no signature check), and its rejection test is !validated && expiring-within-1h — so a token carrying a far-future exp appears to pass with any refresh string. develop rewrote it to validate the signature and reject hard. Recorded as a reading of the source rather than a confirmed exploit, and as one more reason the durable credential is the key and not the pair.

nodes.label: DownloadsService (<documents>/downloads/<profile>/<chapterId>/)
nodes.rationale: One extension-less file per page with meta.json written LAST, so a chapter directory without one is a partial download and is deleted on the next scan(). The <profile> segment is Profile.id percent-encoded — reversible by eye and, unlike a hash, unable to land two people in one directory; filed by chapter id alone one person's saved chapter was listed, readable and progress-writing in the other's session. scan() also deletes any all-digits chapter directory sitting in the root, which is the flat layout this replaced, so a fixture must be written through the service or it is swept and the test is vacuous.

nodes.label: AsyncValue.isResolvedFailure
nodes.rationale: AsyncValue.value is null for both a slow answer and a resolved failure, so a widget drawing a Skeleton whenever it has no value shimmers for an answer that is never coming — the same forever-redraw by another route. hasError && !hasValue, named once so no section can forget it; draw nothing and let the app bar's indicator say why.

nodes.label: kavitaClientProvider
nodes.rationale: Watches only the session's identity (Profile.id, apiKey), not its tokens, since the client patches its own token on renewal and rebuilding here would invalidate every data provider mid-read. It keeps the previous client alive across a session ending — but per container: a static keep-alive handed the previous profile's client to the fresh container a handover builds, a window onto the wrong session on exactly the device this feature is for.

nodes.label: _OfflineHome (an empty state, not the banner returning)
nodes.norm_label: _offlinehome (an empty state, not the banner returning)
nodes.rationale: Drawn when every home provider has resolved into a failure and the device is offline: a screen with nothing on it, in words of its own, naming the one tab that still has something. The teal button appears only where it leads somewhere, so a device holding nothing is told plainly rather than handed a way onto an empty tab — which is why it reads the downloads at all. No icon, because the bar already carries the struck-through cloud.

nodes.label: OfflineIndicator (a status in the app bar, not a banner)
nodes.norm_label: offlineindicator (a status in the app bar, not a banner)
nodes.rationale: A banner is a paragraph: it pushed the shelves down, said the same sentence on three screens at once, and was as loud on the twentieth glance as the first. The sentence survives as the icon's tooltip and semantics label and as a SnackBar on tap, because a struck-through cloud says nothing to a screen reader. Its test harness must build the client with overrideWith, since onReachabilityChanged is wired by the real provider and a ready-made client leaves the indicator dead.

nodes.label: Profile.id = (baseUrl, accountId)
nodes.rationale: The address because a Kavita user id is only unique on its own server, the account id because two people share one address, and not the username because someone who renames themselves in Kavita is the same person. Read out of the session's own token (the nameid claim) rather than asked for, so it is there on a resume; a token with no readable id falls back to the name, which costs exactly the rename the key exists to survive.

nodes.label: serverRetry (bounded provider retries)
nodes.rationale: Riverpod 3 retries with exponential backoff and no ceiling — right for a blip, wrong for being offline: three home providers made 3 then 33 requests a minute, each attempt remounting a repeating Skeleton so the device redrew at ~89fps on a screen showing nothing. Bounded to three attempts inside ~600ms; coming back online is the user's move. kavitaClientProvider keeps its own retry => null because its StateError is control flow, not a failure.

nodes.label: SessionScope (entering a profile rebuilds the whole app)
nodes.norm_label: sessionscope (entering a profile rebuilds the whole app)
nodes.rationale: Owns the ProviderContainer and builds a fresh one from the device-owned overrides when the profile is replaced. The teardown is deliberate rather than selective precisely because a list of profile-scoped providers to invalidate keeps growing and a forgotten entry reads as one person seeing another's library — nothing is listed, so nothing can be left off. Entering starts the app over, not leaving; returning to the same profile keeps its container.

nodes.label: DownloadsNotifier must re-read state.value after an await
nodes.norm_label: downloadsnotifier must re-read state.value after an await
nodes.rationale: A second pill tapped during the first scan() resumes first and writes its own entry, so building the next state on the stale snapshot drops it — leaving a download running that nothing on screen tracks and a pill offering to start it again over the files already being written.

nodes.label: No migration into the profiles storage layout
nodes.norm_label: no migration into the profiles storage layout
nodes.rationale: Neither earlier layout can say which account its key belongs to — that id only ever arrives in a token — so a migrated profile would carry the name-based fallback id and be created again at its next sign-in. Deleting is also the safer half: each old key is a whole Kavita account and has no business staying in the keychain.

nodes.label: A profile has two verbs: switch and remove
nodes.norm_label: a profile has two verbs: switch and remove
nodes.rationale: There is no deliberate sign-out: what it produced — remembered but signed out — is a state a refused key produces on its own, and signOut survives only for onSessionExpired. Removal lives in Settings rather than on the picker, because the picker stands in front of every session and asks for nothing, so a long press there let anybody remove anybody. Settings manages every remembered profile, or a household would sign into each person in turn to tidy up and a profile nothing can sign into could never be removed at all.

nodes.label: ConnectionFailureKind.blockedByBrowser
nodes.rationale: A browser reports a CORS refusal and an absent host through the same XHR error event, and calling that 'unreachable' told someone on a public HTTPS domain to check their LAN. Refusal is the ordinary case: Kavita's production CORS policy names no origin at all, so Access-Control-Allow-Origin is sent to nobody. onWeb defaults to kIsWeb and is a parameter only so the branch can be driven from a test.

nodes.label: ConnectionFailure (connection_failure.dart)
nodes.rationale: Turns a DioException into the few cases that change what someone would do next rather than printing a type, a URI and a socket error. Kavita answers every credential-side failure of login with a bare 401 in the server account's locale, so one message covers six causes; a 200 carrying someone else's HTML fails in the decode and arrives as 'unknown' with no response attached; a self-signed certificate never produces badCertificate but a HandshakeException that also lands in 'unknown'; and 403 is a case of its own because the same classifier reports a refused scan.

nodes.label: _PatraShell._labelsFit (the bottom bar measures its labels)
nodes.rationale: French labels are much longer than English ones and a large system font overflows the bar, so when they do not fit in their share of the width the bar falls back to icons plus tooltips. PatraText.navLabel must stay the single definition of that style, or the measurement and the theme disagree and the check is meaningless.

nodes.label: StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack (four tabs)
nodes.rationale: /series/:id and /reader/:chapterId are declared outside the shell so they are full-screen. Use context.push() to drill down — it gives the back arrow and correct Android back behaviour — and context.go() only for switching branch or login/logout redirects; go for drill-down makes the system back button exit the app.

nodes.label: Kavita (self-hosted server)
nodes.rationale: A self-hosted Kavita is usually a bare IP on the LAN with no certificate, which drives cleartext HTTP, multi-server login and offline behaviour throughout the app.

nodes.label: Patra (Flutter Kavita client)
nodes.rationale: A Flutter mobile client (iOS + iPadOS + Android) for a self-hosted Kavita manga/comics/book server; Linux desktop is enabled purely as a fast local dev target, not a shipped platform.

nodes.label: Cleartext HTTP permitted on both platforms
nodes.norm_label: cleartext http permitted on both platforms
nodes.rationale: Android's config only permits cleartext for hosts written down at build time, which a client of a user-named server cannot know, and iOS's narrower NSAllowsLocalNetworking has a scope Apple states inconsistently. Permitting cleartext is not the same decision as trusting a user-installed CA: trust anchors stay system-only, so a self-signed HTTPS server is still refused.

nodes.label: android.permission.INTERNET in the main manifest
nodes.rationale: Flutter's template declares it only in src/debug and src/profile, so a release build shipped with no network at all and every request failed at the connection — indistinguishable from a server that is down. CI now unzips the bundle and greps its protobuf manifest with grep -qa.

nodes.label: The login form validates the address itself
nodes.norm_label: the login form validates the address itself
nodes.rationale: Uri.hasScheme is not enough: 'kavita.local:5000' parses with a scheme of kavita.local and used to reach dio as an unreadable error. The scheme must be http or https and the host non-empty.

nodes.label: The graphify union merge driver (two halves)
nodes.community_name: The graphify union merge driver (two halves)
nodes.norm_label: the graphify union merge driver (two halves)
nodes.rationale: .gitattributes names the driver and is tracked; the command behind the name lives in the clone's own git config, which is not cloned and cannot be committed — so a clone with only the first half falls back to an ordinary conflict, silently, at the one moment the driver was meant to help. test/graphify_merge_driver_test.dart asserts the attribute and that the graph is tracked, and only where graphify is on PATH that the driver is registered and its pinned absolute interpreter still exists, which a pyenv or uv upgrade moves out from under it. Every failure is local setup, fixed by graphify hook install.

nodes.label: graphify-out/graph.json is committed
nodes.community_name: The graphify union merge driver (two halves)
nodes.rationale: It is what a graphify query reads and rebuilding it costs an LLM run, so it is tracked — which makes two branches that each rebuilt it meet as a conflict in tens of thousands of lines of machine-written JSON. Only what cost something to make is tracked: the graph, GRAPH_REPORT.md and the community labels; the caches, manifest.json, cost.json, the viewer and the machine dotfiles are not.

nodes.rationale: Issues live as GitHub issues in rbioteau/patra, driven through the gh CLI; documented in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.

nodes.norm_label: signing written into the runner target's release.xcconfig

nodes.label: KavitaClient._bearerIsIrrelevant
nodes.rationale: An extra flag keeping the version request out of the ordinary failure domain: _onError would read its 401 as a stale JWT, spend a refresh, replay a request that must 401 again, and fire onSessionExpired — signing the user out over a version string.

nodes.label: Credential (sealed password-or-authKey type)
nodes.rationale: LoginDto carries all three fields flat and so cannot say 'one or the other, never both, never neither' — with two optional strings, sending nothing was a legal call. KavitaClient._loginBody is the single place that flattens it back, and the empty field is how the server knows which path this is.

nodes.label: imageCacheKey (one cover fetched once per household)
nodes.norm_label: imagecachekey (one cover fetched once per household)
nodes.rationale: Every image URL carries the auth key as a query parameter and cached_network_image keys on the URL, so four profiles downloaded and stored the same artwork four times under the one budget they share. The key is the URL with the credential taken out. What makes it safe rather than merely cheap: the app only ever builds an image URL for content the server has already listed for the profile asking, so a restricted cover is never requested and never cached. A screen that guessed an id would break that and would be the thing to fix.

nodes.label: KavitaClient (lib/src/api/kavita_client.dart)
nodes.rationale: Wraps only the endpoints the app uses. On a 401 it mints a new JWT from the auth key — a login, not a refresh — and retries; only a bare 401 from that renewal may end the session, since onSessionExpired now deletes the one secret the profile is remembered by.

nodes.label: lib/src/api/models.dart (defensive DTO parsing)
nodes.rationale: Parsing is defensive (?? defaults) because Kavita omits null fields; keep new types minimal, mapping only the fields actually used. The same defensiveness is what swallows a mistyped key into a plausible default, which is why the contract oracle exists.

nodes.label: test/openapi_contract_test.dart (the spec as an oracle)
nodes.rationale: Catches the one class of mistake nothing else can: a mistyped key makes every EPUB row tappable or a comic library say 'chapitre' without throwing. The field list is derived by reading models.dart, never listed, because a list is where such a check rots; enum values are looked up by value and never by position, since SeriesSortField is one-based where the other filter enums are zero-based. It deliberately does not assert required/nullable, response content types or status codes, because the spec is not good enough at any of them. A missing spec fails the suite rather than skipping it.

nodes.label: Profile (baseUrl, accountId, username, auth key)
nodes.rationale: A server is an address and a profile is one person's account on it, so a family tablet is several profiles at one address. It never carries a password and never the JWT; an empty apiKey means 'remembered but signed out', which is what hasCredential reports.

nodes.label: serverVersionProvider (GET /api/Plugin/version)
nodes.rationale: A second request on purpose: /api/Server/server-info-slim is admin-only, and UserDto.kavitaVersion is ignored because a session resumed offline never got an answer and a server upgraded mid-session would leave it stale — the very case the card exists to catch. Displayed verbatim and attributed; every 'we do not know' renders as no line at all. Folding it into the reachability probe is the tidy-up to resist, since a 404 or 401 comes from a server that is plainly up.

nodes.label: SignInExpired
nodes.rationale: A type of its own because resume is what saw the 401 and the screen must not re-derive it from state it did not throw. It gets connectionSignInExpired rather than the bad-credentials message: nothing the person typed was rejected, because nothing they typed was sent.

nodes.label: suggestsLock (the suggestion goes to the unrestricted profile)
nodes.norm_label: suggestslock (the suggestion goes to the unrestricted profile)
nodes.rationale: Kavita's age restriction protects the account it is set on and does nothing once a child is reading inside an adult's session, so the thing worth a PIN is the session that opens everything. An administrator counts as unrestricted whatever rating is set, because a Kavita admin can edit any restriction including their own — reading it as protection would be reading a fence somebody can open from the inside.

nodes.label: ChapterDto.sortOrder is the reading order
nodes.rationale: Not the order of the JSON array; the server sorts every list it builds on it, and so must we.

nodes.label: POST /api/Series/all-v2 and allSeriesForLibrary paging
nodes.rationale: The body is a filter of enum values checked against the spec's own names; limitTo: 0 stays a literal because 'no limit' is server behaviour the spec never states. The endpoint silently caps at the page size, so the client pages until a short page comes back — a single call would truncate a library at 100 series.

nodes.label: ADR-0001 reader magnify gesture
nodes.rationale: Records what each of three rejected answers felt like and why 2.5x/400pt was chosen; the prototype is kept on the prototype/reader-loupe-gesture branch.

nodes.label: ADR-0003 (a server is an address, a profile is a person)
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003 (a server is an address, a profile is a person)
nodes.rationale: The decision that a family tablet is several profiles at one address, ending on the asymmetry that Kavita's age restriction protects the account it is set on and not a session.

nodes.label: ADR-0004 (the refresh-token pair is gone)
nodes.rationale: Says why the refresh-token pair is gone, why /api/Plugin/authenticate is not used instead, and that each profile's auth key is a complete non-expiring Kavita account credential — which is what the lock's copy has to stay exact about.

nodes.label: Domain docs (single-context CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/)
nodes.rationale: One CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/ at the repo root; documented in docs/agents/domain.md.

nodes.label: Vendored OpenAPI spec (docs/openapi/kavita-openapi-<version>.json)
nodes.rationale: Refreshed by hand and named after its own info.version, asserted by the contract test because the copy that first arrived was named 9.0.2 while describing 0.9.0.0.

nodes.label: One credential, two mechanisms (the account auth key)
nodes.norm_label: one credential, two mechanisms (the account auth key)
nodes.rationale: The apiKey from the login response (Kavita's non-expiring opds key) is the only secret persisted and does three jobs: authenticating image URLs as a query parameter (an cannot always send a header), signing a remembered profile back in with no password, and minting the JWT every other request carries. The JWT is session state and is never written down, so a stored profile always has a key and never a token.

nodes.label: The Kavita client is deliberately hand-written
nodes.norm_label: the kavita client is deliberately hand-written
nodes.rationale: The spec describes 485 operations and 319 schemas while the app calls 22 paths, so ~90% of a generated surface would be dead code. Swashbuckle output declares every int/bool/DateTime non-nullable and not required, so a generator emits models that either crash on an unread series or are nullable everywhere. There are zero operationIds, /api/Reader/image declares no content, every operation declares only 200, and the declared security scheme (x-api-key header) is not what this app sends.

nodes.label: The lock's copy refuses the sentence it would be easiest to write
nodes.norm_label: the lock's copy refuses the sentence it would be easiest to write
nodes.rationale: It keeps people who share this device out of each other's profiles; it is not protection for a lost or stolen device, because each profile's auth key is a complete non-expiring Kavita credential only its owner can rotate, and the saved pages are ordinary files.

nodes.label: resume: three failures are three different facts
nodes.norm_label: resume: three failures are three different facts
nodes.rationale: Signing in again with the stored key means reopening works however long the app was closed, with no clock and no password. Unreachable is not a refused credential — offline there is nothing to ask, so the server is opened on the key it holds. A bare 401 is the key itself being refused and is the only answer that means that. Anything else leaves the key alone, because throwing away a working credential over a 500 would cost a password for a fault that fixes itself.

nodes.label: AuthState.atLaunch
nodes.rationale: A device remembering more than one profile arrives with nobody active and lands on the picker: a shared tablet has no last reader, only a previous one, and opening in their session is how one person's page turn moves another's place. Applied here rather than in SessionStorage.load (which stays a faithful read) or in AuthNotifier.build (which would make a two-profile session unconstructible in a test). It also takes the locked ids, so a lone locked profile is left signed out.

nodes.label: reading_settings.dart / locale_settings.dart as device defaults
nodes.rationale: They keep the flat keys they always wrote, which is what makes this an upgrade nobody notices: a device set before it held profiles keeps every setting for everybody until somebody chooses otherwise for themselves. Nothing is synced to the server deliberately — Kavita keeps preferences of its own and none is the reading direction.

nodes.label: DeviceBiometrics (lib/src/lock/biometrics.dart)
nodes.rationale: biometricOnly: true, because letting the platform fall back to the device passcode would put the one secret everybody already knows in front of a profile. Availability is getAvailableBiometrics().isNotEmpty and not canCheckBiometrics, which is true of a phone whose owner never registered a finger and would draw a key that fails every time. Every call is guarded: no sensor, a missing plugin and a refused prompt all mean 'use the PIN'.

nodes.label: isLaunchProvider
nodes.rationale: A resume is not a launch, and nor is a handover: entering another profile rebuilds the whole app, so the animation would unfurl the frond over somebody who just tapped their own face. False in every container after the first, and LaunchAnimation then never starts its controller — which is why dispose only disposes one where there was something to play.

nodes.label: LaunchStage / launch_composition.dart
nodes.rationale: The handoff's patra-launch.jsx transcribed beat for beat as a pure function of authored time, so the timeline can be read and pinned without a widget tree. Five beats over 7.8s; the numbers are the design's, not ours to round.

nodes.label: LaunchAnimation
nodes.rationale: Wraps the whole app from MaterialApp.builder rather than being a route, because the last beat needs the frond flying and the app it flies into laid out underneath; keeping the app mounted also means its first requests are answered while the splash plays, so the shelves that fade up are real. The splash is outside every Material, so a Material(type: transparency) is what supplies a real DefaultTextStyle.

nodes.label: LaunchSlot registry (LaunchLogoSlot, LaunchWordmarkSlot)
nodes.rationale: Screens put themselves in and are looked up by render box rather than a global key handed down, because a route transition can have two mounted for a frame — which a single global key answers with a crash. The frond's bounds are flown onto the mark slot's rect, not the tile's, or the mark lands high. Everything is measured through the frame actually laid out, the one before the tick doing the measuring.

nodes.label: PatraMasthead (the gate-screen lockup)
nodes.rationale: One widget for the picker and the sign-in form, because the outro lands on whichever is up and a spacing that drifted between them would show as a shift at exactly that moment. Its gap is the one number that does not scale: 0.65em against the header's 0.81em, since what is held constant is that mark and word read as one thing, not the ratio.

nodes.label: PatraWordmark
nodes.rationale: One definition of the word, because the launch animation lands its own on the other two and tracking that drifted would show at the one moment they are compared directly.

nodes.label: PendingLink (a link waits for a profile)
nodes.norm_label: pendinglink (a link waits for a profile)
nodes.rationale: A link names content and a profile names who is reading, and identity comes first: followed as it arrives a link would open in whichever session was last used. So go_router's initial location is not followed and defaultRouteName is read into a PendingLink. It is pushed, not returned, because a returned redirect replaces the stack and would open the app into a room with no door. Only a launch may fill one, or a session ending would push person A's screen at person B; and it is seeded per router only where isLaunchProvider is true.

nodes.label: Profile lock (lib/src/lock/profile_lock.dart)
nodes.rationale: A salted SHA-256 of a four-digit PIN keyed by Profile.id. The hash is not what makes it hard to break — four digits is ten thousand guesses, and anything that can read that row can read the auth key beside it, worth incomparably more. What it buys is that a PIN somebody also uses on a bank card does not sit legible in a file. Enforced in exactly one place, the picker's _enter, before the key is spent — so it is asked offline too.

nodes.label: The profile picker (/profiles)
nodes.rationale: Never appears on a timer: the ways here are opening the app, the face on the Home bar and the server card in Settings, all doing the same switchProfile. Everything it draws comes off the Profile — a cached avatar or the initial on Kavita's own account colour — because it must draw before the first request and often without one succeeding. The only thing that reaches the network is a tap. It never validates keys in the background, which would make this screen ask a server.

nodes.label: ProfileAvatar and _FaceBadge
nodes.rationale: Lives in widgets/ rather than the feature because the same face goes in the Home bar. A refused key is dimmed, badged with a struck-through key in patraAccent and worded, because the handoff's rule is that a cost is always worded and never icon-only and a glyph says nothing to a screen reader. Accent rather than danger: nothing has gone wrong, the profile still opens, and what it costs is a password. A lock badge shares the same corner and the two can never collide.

nodes.label: signedOutLocation (routes.dart)
nodes.rationale: No profile gets the form; exactly one profile needing a password gets the form prefilled, because being asked a question with one answer is a tap that device never had to make; everything else gets the picker. /login stays always reachable while signed out, since adding a profile and signing a refused one back in are reached from the picker. The router's refreshListenable watches the profile count as well as the session.

nodes.label: The language is the only preference written twice
nodes.norm_label: the language is the only preference written twice
nodes.rationale: It is also the only preference read where there is no person: the picker and the sign-in form are drawn before anybody is chosen, and there is no screen on which to set the gate's language. So choosing a language moves the device default too, and a profile that has since chosen for itself is unaffected because its own choice is looked up first.

nodes.label: The OS launch screen is the ink and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: the os launch screen is the ink and nothing else
nodes.rationale: A mark painted by the window would appear, vanish at Flutter's first frame and rebuild itself; what has to be continuous from cold start is the ink, not the logo. Android 12+ points windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon at a deliberately transparent drawable, because the system always composites something and reaches for the launcher icon when the attribute is unset.

nodes.label: The outro adapts to the screen it lands on, not to a flag
nodes.norm_label: the outro adapts to the screen it lands on, not to a flag
nodes.rationale: The presence of a slot is both the question and the answer, so nothing in the animation asks whether a server is configured or which gate the device landed on — which is what made adding the picker cost the animation nothing.

nodes.label: Blades are turned like pages, not grown in place
nodes.norm_label: blades are turned like pages, not grown in place
nodes.rationale: Each blade starts flat out at -72° — the same place for all five — swings to its own angle and is drawn narrower while it travels (0.18 + 0.82·turn^0.8), so it foreshortens across the spine. That is what makes five identical sweeps read as pages rather than a flower opening.

nodes.label: No invite flow is shipped
nodes.community_name: ADR-0003 — A profile is a Kavita account, and there are no local ones
nodes.rationale: Cost accepted: someone must be Kavita admin and create an account per person. POST /api/Account/invite returns a setup link and works without SMTP (InviteUserResponse carries emailLink as well as emailSent), but ConfirmEmailDto { email, token, password, username } needs the invitee to open that link and set their own password in a browser. So family setup leaves the app, and we ship no part of an invite flow rather than half of one.

nodes.label: A replay journal is the real fix (future work)
nodes.norm_label: a replay journal is the real fix (future work)
nodes.rationale: An append-only queue of progress written offline; its own piece of work, and the one future store that would not be discardable — which is what would finally argue for a database.

nodes.label: meta.json — the fragment the device already remembered
nodes.norm_label: meta.json — the fragment the device already remembered
nodes.rationale: Each saved chapter's meta.json holds libraryId, seriesId, volumeId, chapterId, seriesName, title, pages and pagesRead — enough to reach a saved chapter and not enough to navigate: no library name, no library type, no cover, no sibling chapters.

nodes.label: The entry round trip is hidden by the launch animation
nodes.norm_label: the entry round trip is hidden by the launch animation
nodes.rationale: Cost accepted: entering a profile online needs one request before anything works. The launch animation runs 7.8s with the app mounted from the first frame precisely so its first requests are made and answered while the splash plays. Offline no request is made, because a profile entered offline reads only what it has saved.

nodes.label: Cache-first overlay precedence rule
nodes.rationale: Read through an overlay provider per list with one precedence rule: live wins; otherwise stored data draws as data, not as loading; otherwise the live error; otherwise loading. Cost accepted: a stale list is drawn as if current for the second or so before the refresh lands — the same staleness the app already accepts everywhere else (a library is only as current as its last scan, isAdmin only as fresh as the last sign-in).

nodes.label: The per-profile catalogue
nodes.rationale: The libraries, the series in them, and the volumes, chapters and description of every series that has been opened — files under <documents>/catalogue/<profile>/ as spine.json, series/<id>.json and ondeck.json, written from our own models' toJson behind a version stamp that discards rather than migrates. A third store alongside saved chapters and the image cache, which the docs insist must not be confused.

nodes.label: A cover is never pinned; the answer is a real placeholder
nodes.norm_label: a cover is never pinned; the answer is a real placeholder
nodes.rationale: Covers stay in the image cache, one copy per device, so a stored series list routinely outlives the pictures of it. The placeholder is the cover's radius, a 45° hatch in two tones derived from the series id, and the series' initial in the serif — the app's existing answer to 'no picture of this thing' on the picker. Pinning would fork imageCacheKey into a copy per profile, or put a hole in the trim sweep's budget.

nodes.label: drift (rejected, but not for the usual reason)
nodes.norm_label: drift (rejected, but not for the usual reason)
nodes.rationale: drift 2.34.4 runs under flutter test via NativeDatabase.memory(), needs no apt package on ubuntu-latest since it moved to Dart build hooks, and its destructiveFallback is exactly the discard policy — so 'a database costs the test suite' is stale and is not the reason. What rejects it is CI cost: build_runner codegen nothing here uses, a sqlite3 build hook that downloads a prebuilt SQLite from GitHub releases at build time (a network dependency on the Android job, the iOS job and every release tag), and iOS code assets carrying no debug symbols, which surfaces as an App Store Connect upload warning — a poor trade for an option with no buyer in a pipeline whose recovery hatch is a workflow_dispatch at a tag.

nodes.label: Files, not a database
nodes.rationale: A database's decisive advantage is querying a collection without loading it, and nothing here asks for that: search is Kavita's job over the API, EPUB progress and bookScrollId are one small value per chapter, collections and reading lists have the shape libraries and series already have, and a replay journal is an append-only queue. The option stays cheap because the catalogue is the one store whose data is worthless — every byte refetchable — so swapping files for a database later costs the write path and nothing else.

nodes.label: hive_ce (the near-free alternative, rejected)
nodes.rationale: Pure Dart, no native libraries, Hive.init in a test — a defensible answer that buys typed boxes, atomic writes and no whole-file rewrites, but no queries, which makes it files with an index. Files won on having nothing to add to pubspec.yaml.

nodes.label: isResolvedFailure means something new
nodes.rationale: It has meant 'draw nothing, the app bar says why'; it now means 'draw nothing if the catalogue has nothing either'. Where the catalogue is empty — a first launch offline, a library never opened — today's screens stand untouched, so the change is additive.

nodes.label: Only a complete answer replaces
nodes.rationale: allSeriesForLibrary pages until a short page comes back; a run that fails on page 3 must not replace 250 stored series with 200, or the store loses exactly what it exists to keep.

nodes.label: Realm Flutter, Isar, ObjectBox (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Realm Flutter reached EOL on 2025-09-30, Isar has had no stable release since April 2023, and ObjectBox needs install.sh before it runs on the Dart VM.

nodes.label: The catalogue overlays progress rather than absorbing it
nodes.norm_label: the catalogue overlays progress rather than absorbing it
nodes.rationale: _saveProgress mirrors into the saved copy and posts on a queue whose failure is swallowed, so the server never learns what was read on a train. The series screen therefore shows the saved copy's true progress while the grid shows the server's last word. Absorbing it would make every screen agree offline and then walk visibly backwards on reconnect, when the server's older answer replaces it.

nodes.label: Split by level, under documents
nodes.rationale: Split by level rather than one file per profile because sizes matter: a 2000-series library is ~500KB and a series' volumes ~50KB, so one file per profile would rewrite megabytes every time a series is opened. Under documents rather than the system cache directory because a store the OS may silently empty cannot be the thing that makes navigation consistent — that is what the image cache already is.

nodes.label: sqflite (wrong shape regardless)
nodes.rationale: Its own docs say testing with flutter_test is unsupported, and the workaround needs sqflite_common_ffi with a separate databaseFactoryFfiNoIsolate for testWidgets — which is nearly every test here.

nodes.label: Version stamp that discards rather than migrates
nodes.norm_label: version stamp that discards rather than migrates
nodes.rationale: Every byte of the catalogue is refetchable, which is why a version mismatch discards it rather than migrating — and is what makes 'we can change our minds later', normally a lie about persistence, true here: a migration nobody has to write, against data nobody would miss.

nodes.label: featuredSeries (continue_hero.dart)
nodes.rationale: The Continue hero is picked out of the On deck answer, which is one request for both the hero and the shelf and so cannot disagree with itself.

nodes.label: markChapterRead (mark-multiple-read / -unread)
nodes.rationale: There is no single-chapter unread endpoint, and that pair takes one body shape for both directions. The stored copy's progress is mirrored alongside, or the Downloads tab would disagree with no server to ask.

nodes.label: readOverridesProvider (optimistic progress writes)
nodes.rationale: Laid over the fetch so the row redraws on the gesture rather than the round trip; re-fetching would be worse than slow, since the screen pattern-matches AsyncData and any invalidate drops the whole list to its skeleton. A refused write clears the override. autoDispose, so the next visit is the server's word again, and _open clears the chapter's override because reading is about to define progress properly.

nodes.label: entryUnderWay / resume_point.dart
nodes.rationale: What a hero pictures is the chapter it is inside: the predicate the series hero used to decide whether to draw a page behind itself, hoisted into the file that decides where reading resumes, so neither hero can pick a different chapter. A volume with no chapter breakdown is drawn by its volume cover, the choice the rows already make, or the shared URL-keyed cache would store a second copy. The ring follows the picture.

nodes.label: lib/src/theme.dart (design tokens and shared primitives)
nodes.rationale: Holds every token (colors, radii, spacing, type scale) plus SectionLabel, CoverProgressBar and Skeleton. Never hardcode a color or a radius in a screen.

nodes.label: hasReadingProgress (the hero asks about the series)
nodes.norm_label: hasreadingprogress (the hero asks about the series)
nodes.rationale: Finishing a volume leaves the next untouched, so reading progress off the target chapter alone said 'Commencer la lecture' to someone halfway through a series. Kavita's own web client asks the question of the series; the concept appears nowhere in the API, so this mirrors a rule rather than reading a field.

nodes.label: POST /api/Series/on-deck
nodes.rationale: The complement of currently-reading: PagesRead > 0 && PagesRead < Pages with a recent read or added date, so the two are disjoint on the read date and a series read this week is only ever in On deck.

nodes.label: Claude Design handoff (.claude/design/HANDOFF.md)
nodes.rationale: Untracked on purpose, so it is on this machine and absent from a fresh clone. Its §3 and §5 are superseded — §3 by the reader's cog, §5 by the frond icon README and the launch-animation notes.

nodes.label: patraAccent = progress/identity, patraOffline = downloads/offline
nodes.rationale: A hard rule from the handoff: purple means reading progress and identity, teal means downloads and offline, and they must never be swapped.

nodes.label: /api/Series/currently-reading does not mean what it says
nodes.norm_label: /api/series/currently-reading does not mean what it says
nodes.rationale: SeriesFilter.HasReadLast inverts the comparison, so the endpoint returns the series last read MORE than OnDeckProgressDays ago — the pile you abandoned. Promoting the hero from it gave regular readers no hero at all on a Home screen whose shelf listed what they were reading. currentlyReading() is gone from the client and test/home_hero_test.dart asserts the path is never requested.

nodes.label: Serif is only for titles of works, the wordmark and page numerals
nodes.norm_label: serif is only for titles of works, the wordmark and page numerals
nodes.rationale: PatraText.serifTitle (Source Serif 4) is reserved; everything else is Space Grotesk.

nodes.label: Leading = progress, trailing = destruction
nodes.rationale: The two edges never mean the same kind of thing: marking read/unread in patraAccent leads, removing the saved copy in patraDanger trails. Marking needs the server so the leading pane is gone offline, but it does not need a readable format, since a file read elsewhere is exactly what one marks by hand.

nodes.label: ImageCacheStore.trim (a capped image cache)
nodes.rationale: flutter_cache_manager only caps by number of objects, which says nothing about bytes, so the sweep is ours and works on the files directly — safe because the manager re-checks a file exists before serving its row. 'Oldest' is by write time, since atime is unreliable on Android. Runs at startup, when the limit changes, and throttled on every reader page turn, which is where the cache actually grows.

nodes.label: isTabletLayout(context)
nodes.rationale: Asks the shortest side against tabletBreakpoint so a phone in landscape is still a phone — the same question Kavita's own ClientMetrics.isTablet answers.

nodes.label: _PagedView._seeking (a seek is not reported back)
nodes.rationale: jumpToPage dispatches its scroll notification synchronously, so PageView fires onPageChanged from inside the build that delivered the seek. In landscape it reports the first page of the spread, so a seek to an odd page reports a page the reader never asked for and setState runs mid-build — surfacing as 'Each child must be laid out exactly once' with a RenderErrorBox in the Scaffold's body slot. Any programmatic move of a PageController needs the same guard.

nodes.label: _SqueezedByPane
nodes.rationale: Slidable uncovers a pane by translating its whole child, carrying the cover and title the swipe is about to act on off the leading edge. The wrapper works from inside that translation, undoing it and handing the pane's edge the same width as padding, so the row keeps its origin and is merely narrower. Only the pane's width is squeezed out; a further drag keeps the library's slide for the rubber band.

nodes.label: ThumbLoadQueue
nodes.rationale: Thumbnails do not load when built: held 180ms, then at most two at a time, nearest the current page first and only pages on screen — a flick through a 200-page chapter used to fire a request per thumbnail mounted. A failed thumbnail is marked done and never retried. The precache and the widget must ask for the same decode width, since ResizeImage puts it in the cache key and a mismatch precaches one image and displays another.

nodes.label: ThumbStrip (thumb_strip.dart)
nodes.rationale: An accordion keyed to the page being read, so item extents are not uniform. It is drawn at an offset it computes and has no scroll position: jumpTo calls markNeedsLayout, and the page arrives in a build under LayoutBuilders, so dirtying layout from inside layout killed the next frame — deferring only moved it into the phase Flutter documents as having to stay clean. _offset is a function of the accordion's two pages and its clock, so sizes and offset are read from the same state in the same build and cannot disagree (they used to animate apart by 123pt). The bulge travels on the same linear law as the slider handle, because the two sit one above the other. sliderPadding is derived from the thumbnail geometry against Material's 26pt handle inset. Sizes are shares of the screen's shortest side, never points; a tablet takes a smaller share of a wider screen. The one limit in points is a gesture: the chrome must stop short of the middle of the screen, or the tap meant to dismiss it seeks instead. Nothing on the item-builder path may reach back into the reader, since a lazy list builds during layout.

nodes.label: Tap zones 30/40/30 and mirrored right-to-left chrome
nodes.norm_label: tap zones 30/40/30 and mirrored right-to-left chrome
nodes.rationale: Sides page, centre toggles chrome; right-to-left mirrors reverse, the tap meanings, the thumbnail strip and the slider together via Directionality, while page numerals stay left-to-right.

nodes.label: A column of rows runs the full width at the app's gutter
nodes.norm_label: a column of rows runs the full width at the app's gutter
nodes.rationale: The cap at 560 left an 820pt iPad wearing ~150pt of nothing down each side, and a narrow column floating between two empty bands reads worse than the gap it closed. The answer to a tablet's width is a grid, not a narrower column; inside the row the furniture grows instead (rowCoverWidth/rowCoverWidthTablet, one number shared by the series screen and the Downloads tab).

nodes.label: A shelf and the reader canvas run edge to edge
nodes.norm_label: a shelf and the reader canvas run edge to edge
nodes.rationale: A shelf spends a tablet's width on bigger tiles (112 → 152); the reader is left alone because there the whole screen is the point.

nodes.label: A grid of cards takes another column, not a bigger card
nodes.norm_label: a grid of cards takes another column, not a bigger card
nodes.rationale: _gridColumns and _cardWidth divide the width by a max card width with the handoff's phone count as the floor: three covers across an iPad would be 250pt each, five at 146 is the same screen with more of it.

nodes.label: A swipe pane and a button must never scale with the screen
nodes.norm_label: a swipe pane and a button must never scale with the screen
nodes.rationale: A slidable extentRatio that is a sensible drawer on a phone hides the cover and title on a tablet, so _ChapterRow converts a width in points into the ratio; a button given a whole hero stops reading as a button, so resume and sign-out stop at 280.

nodes.label: The reader must never wrap itself in a LayoutBuilder
nodes.norm_label: the reader must never wrap itself in a layoutbuilder
nodes.rationale: OrientationBuilder IS one, and the body fills the window so the MediaQuery already answers. A LayoutBuilder runs the builds of everything beneath it during layout — pages, tap zones, chrome, scrubber, every image frame and every Slider setState — so the screen died on debugNeedsLayout and _debugRelayoutBoundaryAlreadyMarkedNeedsLayout. Read layout information only where genuinely needed, and never around a subtree that rebuilds on animation, images and gestures.

nodes.label: The system's chrome comes and goes with the reader's
nodes.norm_label: the system's chrome comes and goes with the reader's
nodes.rationale: The chapter opens in immersiveSticky and returns to edgeToEdge when the centre tap raises the reader's own bars and again on the way out, so the clock is never over the page but always one tap away. Every path that moves _showChrome goes through _showChromeAndBars or the two drift apart.

nodes.label: _PagedView._reported must be set in initState, not by a late initialiser
nodes.norm_label: _pagedview._reported must be set in initstate, not by a late initialiser
nodes.rationale: A late field runs its initialiser at the first read, which is the comparison in didUpdateWidget where widget.page is already the new page — so it initialised to the value it was about to be tested against and the guard skipped the jump. The first side-zone tap moved the number and left the pager; the second jumped two. Unnoticed because a swipe takes the onPageChanged path, and swiping was how everyone got through a chapter.

nodes.label: Saved chapters and the image cache are two stores
nodes.norm_label: saved chapters and the image cache are two stores
nodes.rationale: Saved chapters live in the documents directory, are chosen by the user and are never evicted. The image cache is cached_network_image's own store in the system cache directory, holding covers and pages merely browsed — it outgrew the downloads three to one on a real device and the OS may reclaim it. Clearing the cache must never touch the documents directory.

nodes.label: Android adaptive icon (drawable/patra_mark.xml)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not generated: a vector cannot pixelate and no generator can rewrite the anydpi-v26 inset to double-pad a vector already carrying padding. Scaled to 0.76 so the bounding box's far corner sits 32.1dp from centre, just inside the 33dp guaranteed-visible radius; the mono variant carries the fan by fillAlpha alone with lifted parchment steps, because the ordering carries the fan rather than the absolute values.

nodes.label: FrondGeometry.boundsOf
nodes.rationale: Blade extremes come off the cap centres grown by the radius, because a capsule has no corners; this is the Dart-side computation the adaptive icon's numbers were derived from.

nodes.label: PatraFrond (lib/src/widgets/patra_frond.dart)
nodes.rationale: The mark itself, shared by the animation and the header, with geometry in the SVG's own 88x88 tile space so the Dart file, the Android vector and the icon bitmaps can be read against one another. Sized by the mark, not the tile. Parchment #E9E2D0 is private to this file and must never appear in the UI.

nodes.label: The palm frond mark (five-blade and compact three-blade)
nodes.norm_label: the palm frond mark (five-blade and compact three-blade)
nodes.rationale: Below about 72px the five blades and their gaps each fall under two pixels and the fan closes into a blob, so every icon at or under 72px is rendered from the compact master. That size rule is why flutter_launcher_icons is gone.

nodes.label: The header draws the five-blade fan at 24pt
nodes.norm_label: the header draws the five-blade fan at 24pt
nodes.rationale: The design's mock put a three-blade mark at ~16pt against a 17px wordmark; at the app's 22pt wordmark that reads as a plain arrow, and the animation would spend two seconds unfurling five blades only to crossfade into three. In the app the mark is painted rather than rasterised, so the answer is to draw it big enough for the fan to stay open.

nodes.label: AuthNotifier.clearAdmin (a 403 clears the flag)
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.rationale: A refusal from an admin-only endpoint is the server's own answer and is fresher than the flag, so the controls it draws stop being drawn until a sign-in says otherwise. The flag is only ever cleared and never set: a 200 from one admin endpoint is not a role.

nodes.label: currentLibraryProvider
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.rationale: One question asked by both the grid and the scan menu so they cannot mean different libraries; the menu item is meaningless while the list is in flight or has failed.

nodes.label: DashedBorderPainter (the mark for a place to fill)
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.norm_label: dashedborderpainter (the mark for a place to fill)
nodes.rationale: Dashed rounded outline means a place to fill (empty library, add-a-server slot), as against solid borders that enclose something already there.

nodes.label: LibraryScanNotifier
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.rationale: A notifier family keyed by library id: one in-flight flag makes the empty-state button and the app-bar menu two entry points to one action, with one wording of the failure. It reports the failure instead of wording it (a notifier has no BuildContext). The grid is invalidated on the empty-state path only, or the menu would drop a populated grid to its skeleton for a background job that has produced nothing.

nodes.label: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.norm_label: userdto.isadmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.rationale: Tests for 'Admin' and fails closed on a missing or malformed list, since guessing yes draws a button that can only fail. Persisted on the Profile because the picker and a session's first frame draw before any request answers, but refreshed on every sign-in rather than frozen — so it is as old as the last successful sign-in, costing an admin a control and never offering a non-admin one.

nodes.label: POST /api/Library/scan (admin only)
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.rationale: Behind Kavita's AdminPolicy (RequireRole Admin), and so is every other way in — scan-folder is [AllowAnonymous] but refuses a non-admin itself. libraryId goes in the query string because the action takes a bare int. The scan is a background job: it is requested, never finished, by the call that returns 200.

nodes.label: Admin scan request from the Library tab's app-bar menu
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.norm_label: admin scan request from the library tab's app-bar menu
nodes.rationale: Worded rather than drawn: a refresh glyph would be taken for pull-to-refresh, which does the opposite job. Drawn only for an administrator, since this app never draws a control that can only earn a 403. Offline it is disabled with its reason rather than hidden, gated on offlineProvider rather than a health probe because being wrong there is self-correcting.

nodes.label: An empty library is a state, not a blank screen
nodes.community_name: UserDto.isAdmin (role read from the login response)
nodes.norm_label: an empty library is a state, not a blank screen
nodes.rationale: A library is empty because the server has not scanned, so the copy points at the server and names the library — picked out of the localized sentence by indexOf rather than concatenated, or a French sentence would be assembled in English word order. It is pullable because after asking for a scan there has to be a way to look again.

nodes.label: readOverridesProvider (optimistic write)
nodes.community_name: ADR-0002 — One rule decides where reading resumes, and it is ours
nodes.rationale: Lays new progress over the fetched volumes so swiping a chapter read moves the resume target on the gesture rather than on the round trip. The server cannot see an optimistic write, so a server-decided target is a round trip behind by definition — adopting continue-point everywhere would regress the series screen.

nodes.label: _SeriesHero._target()
nodes.community_name: ADR-0002 — One rule decides where reading resumes, and it is ours
nodes.rationale: The series screen's original client-side answer to where reading resumes, and the implementation the shared rule was extracted out of.

nodes.label: Home screen Continue hero
nodes.community_name: ADR-0002 — One rule decides where reading resumes, and it is ours
nodes.rationale: Needs the resume answer and the chapter object itself, because it names the chapter and counts the pages left in it. Fetches /api/Series/volumes for its one featured series and runs the shared rule.

nodes.label: GET /api/Reader/continue-point (deliberately uncalled)
nodes.community_name: ADR-0002 — One rule decides where reading resumes, and it is ours
nodes.rationale: Named for exactly this job and returns the one ChapterDto the hero would otherwise find itself, but stays uncalled. The spec's own summary describes a different rule ('the next chapter which has progress') from ours ('the first chapter not fully read'), and the two do not obviously agree with chapter 1 finished and chapter 2 untouched. Whether Kavita's implementation diverges is not knowable from Swashbuckle output, and two screens of one app offering to resume different chapters is too bad an outcome for 'they probably agree'.

nodes.label: GET /api/Series/volumes as the hero's source
nodes.community_name: ADR-0002 — One rule decides where reading resumes, and it is ours
nodes.rationale: Cost accepted: it returns every volume and chapter where continue-point returns one chapter, and it lands on home load. Judged acceptable because it is one request for one featured series (not one per tile) and is the same request the series screen makes the moment the hero's cover is tapped.

nodes.label: Shared resume rule (first chapter not fully read)
nodes.community_name: ADR-0002 — One rule decides where reading resumes, and it is ours
nodes.norm_label: shared resume rule (first chapter not fully read)
nodes.rationale: Order the chapters, take the first one not fully read. Extracted into a single shared function so the series screen and the Continue hero cannot diverge; it is load-bearing on two screens, and changing it changes both — which is the point of the decision rather than a side effect.

nodes.label: Accent-coloured centre blade and stem
nodes.community_name: Compact three-blade frond variant (icons at or under 72px)
nodes.rationale: At every size in this chunk the vertical centre blade plus the short stem below the pivot are painted in the purple patraAccent while the outer blades are parchment-grey. That single coloured element is what survives the downscale: at 40px the outer blades read as little more than a grey chevron and the accent stroke is the only part still clearly identifiable, which is why the accent is on the centre blade rather than distributed across the fan.

nodes.label: 72px master-selection rule for icon rasterisation
nodes.community_name: Compact three-blade frond variant (icons at or under 72px)
nodes.rationale: This chunk straddles the threshold exactly and confirms the rule empirically: the three 1x renders measured 40, 50 and 57 pixels and each shows the three-blade compact mark, while the four 2x/3x renders measured 80, 100, 114 and 120 pixels and each shows the five-blade fan. The rule exists because below about 72px the five blades and the gaps between them each fall under two pixels, so the fan closes into an indistinct blob; rendering the small sizes from the compact master keeps the mark legible. This is also why a single-master generator such as flutter_launcher_icons was abandoned in favour of tool/gen_app_icons.sh, which picks the master by target size.

nodes.label: Opaque ink ground with no alpha channel
nodes.community_name: Compact three-blade frond variant (icons at or under 72px)
nodes.norm_label: opaque ink ground with no alpha channel
nodes.rationale: Every render in this chunk is a square, corner-less, fully opaque sRGB bitmap (no alpha channel reported) on the near-black patra ink ground, with the mark centred and no rounding of its own. App Store Connect rejects an app icon carrying any alpha, and iOS applies the superellipse mask itself, so alpha is stripped on the iOS side of the generator and no corner radius is baked in — the opposite of the Android legacy mipmaps, which do get the platform's 22.7% corner because a pre-API-26 launcher does not add one.
